meta.title: Better Workflows | Your coding agent finishes on current evidence
meta.description: An open-source Claude Code plugin: the agent cannot finish on a stale green test, and cannot repeat or stack side effects whose result it never saw. Permissions come from a policy file, never from the prompt.
meta.imageAlt: Better Workflows control plane illustration: ledger, evidence seals and reconciliation nodes

shell.tagline: Your coding agent finishes on current evidence, and runs each side effect at most once.

hero.lead: A Claude Code plugin that keeps an AI agent from finishing on a stale green test, and from repeating or stacking side effects whose result it never saw. What it may do comes from a policy file you write, never from the prompt.
hero.status: Pre-alpha. Running daily on two of the maintainer's repositories.

principles.title: Three rules that get more useful as models get stronger.
principles.lead: A stronger agent writes more code per session and runs more commands on its own. These rules do not depend on the agent being careful; they hold whatever it says.
pillars: What the agent may push, merge, release or publish comes from a policy file it cannot edit. Asking nicely in the prompt changes nothing.
Evidence is tied to the files
A passing test counts only for the exact files it ran on. Change one line and that pass no longer counts.
Unknown stops, it does not guess
A side effect whose result is unknown blocks every further side effect until it is checked against the provider or settled by a person.
compare: Tests passed, then a file changed
Sent back to rerun on the current files.
Counted as green; the exit code belongs to tail.
One spec file instead of the suite
With exact, only the whole command counts.
Same push at same commit is refused.
Policy decides: allow, ask or deny.
layers: Written and changed by a person. The agent may read it, never edit it.
Still apply. allow in the policy never grants more than Claude Code would.
Enforce the policy on every command, edit and stop.
Describes the goal. Carries no authority.

workflow.title: Four hooks, one ledger in .git.
workflow.lead: Core runs inside Claude Code's own hooks. Nothing to start, no server, no account; state lives in .git/better-workflows/ of each repository.
hooks: SessionStart: loads the policy and warns when something it needs, like gh, is missing.
PreToolUse: allows, asks or denies each side effect, and refuses edits to the policy and the ledger.
PostToolUse: records each check with the Git tree it ran on, and each side effect with its exit code.
Stop: sends the agent back while a required check is missing, failed or stale.
bw status: shows the same state to you.

completion.name: Finishing
completion.body: A test, lint, typecheck or build counts only if it passed, its own exit code decided the line, no file changed while it ran, and the files are still exactly what it ran on.
guards: exact: only the whole command counts, from the right directory.
scope: a change outside the named directories leaves the result fresh.
ignore: output a check writes, like coverage, is not counted as a change.

actions.name: Side effects
actions.body: Pushes, PR creates and merges, releases, package publishes and your own custom kinds each need allow from the policy. Only exit code 0 is a known result.
actions.kindsK: Read-only checks used to settle an unknown result

rules: An invalid policy denies every side effect instead of falling back to defaults.
An expired permission falls back to ask. Only a person extends it, by editing the policy.
Commands Core cannot read, like eval or sh -c, are treated as opaque and asked about.
The ledger is append-only and hash-chained; bw verify detects edits and truncation.

hosts.title: Claude Code first.
hosts.lead: Core is host-neutral; each host needs a small adapter. Claude Code is the first and the only one supported today.
hosts.caption: Host and operating system support
hosts.matrixNote: CI runs Core on every pull request.
hosts.recoBody: Its hooks see every command before it runs and every attempt to stop. That is exactly where Core has to sit.
hosts.recoFoot: Codex, Gemini CLI and Qwen Code ran V5, which is frozen at RC1. They will come back as adapters once Core is stable.

install.title: Three commands, then ask for a change.
install.lead: Needs Node.js 22.14 or later, Git, and Claude Code with plugin support.
steps: Once per machine. If you ran V5 here, move ~/.better-workflows to ~/.better-workflows-V5 first.
Install it per repository with --scope local, so nothing is written into files you commit.
bw init writes .better-workflows/policy.json. Commit it so everyone gets the same rules.
install.stepsNote: The full walkthrough covers your own checks, side effects and unknown results.
install.firstAsk: Change one line in this repository, and don't run the tests.
install.firstNote: When Claude Code tries to finish, it is sent back and told which check is missing.
install.demoNote: Optional: run both stories without Claude, in about 2 seconds.

boundary.title: What it stops, and what it cannot see.
boundary.lead: A gate is only useful if you know its edges.
cols: Finishing on a stale, failed or partial test run
A pipe or || true hiding a failure
A repeated push, merge, release or publish
Side effects while an earlier one is unknown
The agent editing its own policy
See side effects inside a script, unless the policy names that script
Judge whether your tests are good enough
Build a dependency graph: a scope must name everything a check depends on
Count Git-ignored files as part of the evidence
Settling a side effect whose result cannot be read back
Deciding when a session is going in circles
boundary.claim: Core blocks the mistakes above. It has not been measured whether it lowers rework or wrong decisions over long tasks; that is what the current self-use period is for.
rules: The shell parser does not grow: a command it cannot read never counts as evidence and is asked about as an action.
Core only counts how a session is going. Whether it is converging is for the agent or you to judge.
Pull requests and releases are reconciled with gh; without it, they stay unknown until you settle them.

faq.title: Common questions, straight answers.
faq.lead: Something else? Open an issue on GitHub.
items: Does it slow Claude Code down?
Each hook hashes the working tree with Git, which takes milliseconds in a normal repository. Very large repositories pay more on each call.
Will it get stuck sending the agent back forever?
It sends the agent back with the reason and how the session has gone so far: runs, failures in a row, times already sent back. The agent can then stop and tell you plainly which check keeps failing.
Can the agent turn it off?
No. It cannot edit the policy or the ledger, and cannot run bw init or settle an unknown action itself. You can uninstall the plugin at any time.
Does it send anything anywhere?
No. There is no server and no telemetry. Everything stays in your repository's .git folder.
What about Codex, Gemini CLI or Qwen Code?
They ran V5, which is frozen. Core is host-neutral, and adapters for them are planned after the alpha.
